title: Why Shiva has a thousand names
hook: a hungry boy, a sage, and a hymn made of nothing but names: one god, many doors
carry: one god, many names, each one a door
tomorrow: why call a fierce god the kind one?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the secret of Chidambaram: the same lord, with form and as open space. Today, a hymn of names begins.
screen: `THE SAME LORD, WITH FORM AND AS SPACE.` · `A HYMN OF NAMES BEGINS.`

segments.voice: A woman is Mom to her kids, Auntie to her nephew, a last name to her boss, and a nickname to her oldest friend. One person, and every name catches her from a different side. Hindu tradition does this with the divine, on purpose, and at length. Some hymns are nothing but names, one after another, like beads on a string. Today i'll open one of them: the Shiva Sahasranama.
screen: `ONE PERSON, MANY NAMES.` → `A HYMN MADE OF NAMES.` → `THE SHIVA SAHASRANAMA.`

segments.voice: Sahasranama is the hymn's own name for itself: the thousand names. Shiva has more than one such hymn; this one is in the Mahabharata, and it comes with a story. Krishna wants a son, so he climbs to the Himalayan hermitage of an old sage, Upamanyu. And Upamanyu tells him how he found Shiva. As a poor boy in the forest he once tasted milk, and came home begging for more. His mother had none. She stirred flour into water and gave him that, and when he knew the difference, she told him the truth: only Shiva could give him what he longed for. The boy turned to Shiva with his whole life, and in the epic's telling, Shiva came. Now, old, he hands Krishna the gift that costs nothing: the names. Near the start: Sthira, the firm one. Sthanu, the post. Prabhu, the lord. Bhima, the fearsome one. Sthanu is a plain word, a tree stump that doesn't move in the wind, and it sits right beside the dancer who never stops. The names don't argue. They stack. This is a Hindu teaching as old as the Rig Veda: truth is one, and the wise call it by many names. No single name says everything; each one is a door. So at a temple archana, a priest offers a flower at each name, a slow walk through the doors. And at home, the same Shiva might simply be Bholenath, the simple-hearted lord. One god, many names, and a devotee is allowed a favorite.
screen: `SAHASRANAMA: THE THOUSAND NAMES.` · `UPAMANYU: THE BOY WHO WANTED MILK.` · `STHANU: THE STEADY POST.` · `TRUTH IS ONE, CALLED BY MANY NAMES.` · then, large: `EACH NAME A DOOR.`

segments.voice: Choose three names of God you know, from any of these days, or the one your family uses. Say each one slowly, and after each, pause, as if you'd laid a flower down, the way an archana goes. If you pray, let each name be a small offering to Shiva, or to God. If you don't, say three words for what you most need: steady, kind, free, and pause after each.
The Shiva Sahasranama. A hymn of Shiva's names, said one at a time, each name a door into the one lord. Today's name from it: Sthanu, the steady post.
Your line: one god, many names, each one a door. Today's door: Sthanu, the steady post. Rest well.
